label: Whatever causes a quality in another thing is more such than that thing, from reception limits
meaning: Derives the Metaphysics II.1 / Posterior Analytics I.2 premise that a distinct cause of a quality is more such, from six OPEN analyst premises: the cause has what it gives; a perfection caused in another is received in it; reception limits by the recipient; limitation by z is only through reception in z; the cause's perfection is not received in its effect; and an unlimited possessor exceeds a limited one. A distinct cause c of r in x has r; x has r received in x, so limited by x; c's r is not received in x, so not limited by x; hence c is more r than x. It does not use STMT-PERFECTIONS-OF-EFFECT-PREEXIST-IN-CAUSE, so it does not close a cycle with PERFECTION-PREEXISTENCE-FROM-CAUSAL-TRANSFER.

strong_version_needed.376d6a5a-c179-5090-b57c-f9a371222899: The conclusion concerns every distinct cause of any quality in another, not only causes of that thing's being, so the registered cause-of-being restriction (specs/cause-of-being-has-being.toml) does not suffice. The proof uses the principle only for distinct causes: the weaker distinct-cause version suffices and is used by the sibling 'More such from distinct-cause transfer and reception limits' (specs/preexistence-without-transfer.toml); this argument keeps the unrestricted version because its Challenge is frozen.
